notes: Measured on the unit in captures/oneplus-buds-4-2026-10-17. The name is matched exactly against what macOS reports, and the service UUID is the gate every member of the family passes.

evidence.note: The session HELLO is answered with a static 8-byte value, so the control channel is up and the device is answering it.
0x8106: a count then (slot, level) pairs. Levels arrive as multiples of 10 on this unit; the app reports the raw byte.

Measured as a negative: across a full session every 0x8106 reply carried count = 2, left and right, even while the wear reply named slot 3 on every poll. The case's charge reaches the phone app by some path this channel does not show.

caseBattery.note: read: false is the finding, not a gap. The app says the case has not reported a charge rather than drawing an empty percentage.

evidence.note: 0x8109: a count then (slot, placement). Slot 3 names the case, which is the cheapest honest signal that one is present and awake.

Each mask was set and read back one at a time: off 0x0008, transparency 0x0100, adaptive 0x0800, cancellation high 0x0010 / moderate 0x0020 / low 0x0040 / auto 0x0080. The setter writes a 16-bit little-endian mask; the single-byte conveniences the vendor app also has are never sent, because they map to the wrong modes.
0x00 and 0x02 were set and read back. 0x03 is skipped by the firmware entirely; 0x04 is the custom slot.

equalizer.note: The custom slot exists as a preset but cannot be selected until a saved profile does, so this app offers it only when the device reports one. Writing a custom profile is a file transfer and is out of scope.

evidence.note: 0x8124 answers [min][max][current], all signed: this unit reports -5...+5. The setter writes back the bounds it was given, which is why the registry does not restate the range.
The 18 four-byte records behind a count. The setter is the same 18-record table, and this app only offers action codes that have been seen stored.

gestures.note: The in-call context (type 0x06) is deliberately not offered: its action codes are unnamed in every description of this protocol, and guessing between answer and decline risks ending someone's call.

evidence.note: The 0x8112 getter answers with the same body the 0x0204 push carries: a count, then records of [address 6][length][state][flags][nameLength][name]. The SDK's own parser strides by the same length byte, which is what makes the layout more than a fit to one sample.

multipoint.note: writable is false although the vendor SDK does implement a setter (0x0429, operateMultiConnectHandheldDevice). It has never been exercised on this hardware and no capture shows it, so there is no write path here.

evidence.note: The setter exists (0x0400) and its ack (0x8400) has been seen answering with a single result byte. Nothing distinguishes accept from reject on that ack, and no recording of a ring was kept.

findMyEarbuds.note: read: false and writable: false is a deliberate gap against the phone app, which does have a Ring button. Ringing is a write with no read-back and no capture behind it here, so BudsDesk offers none until there is a recording and an ear test. See DECISIONS D5.

evidence.note: 0x8105 answers a comma-separated ASCII string, shown verbatim. It is not a dotted version and this project does not invent one.
0x8114 answers the id the vendor's own list is built from; 02 is AAC by that list. Read-only: the vendor setter (0x041a) changes the phone's link, not the Mac's.
